facts.text: On this date in 1929, the U.S. stock market crashed — but the country that suffered the most unemployment wasn't America. Germany hit 30% joblessness by 1932, helping deliver Hitler his electoral opening.
On this date in 1969, the first message sent over ARPANET crashed after two letters. The intended word was 'LOGIN.' What arrived at Stanford: 'LO.'
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth — not Tokyo, not Dhaka. Its core district packs over 111,000 people per square kilometer, roughly 70 times denser than Los Angeles.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than inside one drawn around the entire continent of Australia.
Canada is the second-largest country by area yet has a smaller population than the state of California — 40 million people spread across nearly 10 million square kilometers.
On this date in 1929, the Dow fell 11.7% in a single session — Black Tuesday. It would take 25 years for the index to fully recover its losses.
On Oct 29, 1987, just two weeks after Black Monday, the Dow rebounded 10.1% in one day. Markets have a habit of their most violent swings clustering together.
The Dutch East India Company peaked at a valuation equivalent to roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars — larger than the entire current US stock market.
Saudi Aramco paid out more in dividends in 2023 than Apple, Microsoft, and Google combined earned in net profit.
The bond market is nearly three times the size of the global stock market, yet it gets a fraction of the coverage. The smarter money has always known where the real action is.

On this date in 1998, John Glenn returned to orbit at 77, and his body re-experienced the same bone density loss and fluid shifts as any 25-year-old astronaut. Aging does not buy immunity from spaceflight.
On this date in 1969, the first message sent over ARPANET crashed after two letters. The intended word was 'login.' The internet's first word was, technically, 'lo.'
Your femur withstands forces up to five times your body weight during a casual jog — making it, pound for pound, stronger than reinforced concrete.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh around a billion tons on Earth.
Mantis shrimp see 16 types of color receptors compared to the human three, yet research shows they are worse at distinguishing similar hues — their brains classify color rather than compare it.
On this day in 1929, the stock market collapsed in what we call Black Tuesday — an event closer in time to the American Civil War than it is to today.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. We tend to imagine the medieval and the pre-Columbian as contemporaries. They weren't.
On this day in 1969, the first message ever sent over ARPANET — the internet's ancestor — crashed after two letters. The intended word was 'login.' History's first text was 'lo.'

The fax machine was invented in 1843, before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and 15 years before the first transatlantic cable. It arrived absurdly early and somehow outlasted almost everything born after it.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Egypt's own ancient history was ancient to the Egyptians.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Too precise to stay invented.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Also Koenig's. Some gaps in language wait centuries to be named; others wait for one careful person with a blog.
On this day in 1929, the New York Stock Exchange collapsed in what became Black Tuesday. The Yiddish word for it came later — fardreyt, meaning dizzied, twisted, spun hopelessly out of true.
On this day in 1969, the first message sent over ARPANET crashed after two letters. The intended word was 'login.' What arrived was 'lo' — accidental, and somehow perfect.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable not because English lacks words, but because English lacks the specific grief of homesickness for the imaginary.
On Oct 29, 2013, the world's first Bitcoin ATM opened in a Vancouver coffee shop. It processed $10,000 in transactions on day one, charging a 3% fee — steep then, quaint now.
On Oct 29, 2021, the Bored Ape Yacht Club floor crossed 40 ETH for the first time. The collection had minted at 0.08 ETH just six months earlier.
Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet holds no coins — only unspent transaction outputs. When you 'send' bitcoin, you destroy old outputs and mint new ones, keeping change.
Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since Aug 2021, burns base fees rather than paying them to miners. Over 4 million ETH had been destroyed by the protocol within its first two years.
The 2016 DAO hack didn't break Ethereum's code — it exploited a reentrancy bug in a third-party contract. The controversial hard fork that reversed it split the chain, creating Ethereum Classic.

Today in history: On October 29, 1969, the first message sent over ARPANET crashed after two letters. The internet's ancestor failed at 'LOGIN.' Neural networks now process more data in a second than that entire network handled in its first year.

Today in history: In October 2015, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo secretly defeated European champion Fan Hui 5-0 — months before any public announcement. The AI community didn't know the game had already changed.

The GPT-4 training run consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. homes. That buys one model with no guaranteed understanding of anything.

Transformers, now the dominant architecture in AI, were introduced in 2017 by eight Google researchers. The paper was titled 'Attention Is All You Need.' Six of the eight authors have since left Google.
RLHF — the technique that made ChatGPT usable — relies partly on human labelers in low-wage markets rating model outputs for harm. The alignment of frontier AI runs through a Kenyan data center.
